To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combined CYP1A2 (C–344T) T/T genotype and the CYP1B2 (C–444T) T/T and CYP2D6 (Glu486Gly) G/G genotype were significantly associated with HNSCC in smokers and that the combined C/T genotype of CYP1A (T–309C) C/T was a risk factor in nonsmokers.
the CYP1B gene is associated with HNSCC, especially with the CYP1b1 (Leu 432 Val) C/G genotype.

the risk of HNSCC in nonsmokers was significantly associated with ERCC2 (K751Q) C/C genotype, whereas in smokers the risk of HNSSC was significantly associated with the combination of CYP1A2 (A/C) C/C and C/A genotypes, CYP1A (A/C) A/A genotype, CYP1D (G/T) G/G genotype, and CYP1B (L432V) G/G genotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of polymorphic enzymes of tobacco smoke metabolism and repair in HNSCC.
the identification and quantification of genetic factors that contribute to individual differences in susceptibility to HNSSC.
the impact of polymorphisms in genes encoding xenobiotic metabolism enzymes and repair enzymes on the risk for HNSCC in smokers and nonsmokers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of genetic factors on the risk of HNSCC is complex, and the role of polymorphisms in xenobiotic metabolizing genes and DNA repair genes is not yet clear.
the data support a role of genetic predispositions in enzymes involved in metabolism and repair of tobacco smoke carcinogens in the development of HNSCC.
the data do not allow to make a statement on the role of polymorphic genes in HNSCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CYP1B and GSTM1 are relevant for susceptibility in smokers and ERCC2 is relevant for susceptibility in nonsmokers.

the risk for HNSCC is influenced by the genotype of the polymorphic ERCC2 (XPD) Lys751Gln, CYP1A2 (–163C>A) A allele, CYP1C1 (Ile462Val) A allele, GSTM1 null allele, and XRCC3 (Thr241Met) A allele in nonsmokers and by the genotype of CYP1A, CYP2A6, CYP1E, GSTM
CYP1B, CYP2B, and ERCC2 are relevant in HNSCC carcinogenesis in nonsmokers, whereas CYP1B and GSTM1 are relevant in HNNCC carcinogenesis in smokers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the impact of polymorphic genes in the carcinogenesis and development of HNSCC is complex, and the effects of polymorphisms in the genes encoding enzymes of xenobiotics metabolism and repair are not independent from each other.
the impact of polymorphic genes of metabolism and repair on susceptibility to HNSC is dependent on tobacco smoking.

genetic predisposition and environmental exposure interact in the development of HNSCC and that these interactions should be taken into account for individual risk assessments and for the design of future studies.
